title: Relative completeness of Kleene induction for the positive calculus of relations
formal: Is every equation valid in binary relations with union, intersection, composition, converse, constants \(0,1,\top\), and reflexive-transitive closure derivable from all valid closure-free equations in these operations together with the Kleene algebra axioms and induction rules specified below?
why: This asks whether standard induction for iteration remains complete when programs can also be intersected and reversed as binary relations. A positive theorem would give a principled relative proof calculus for graph reachability expressions; a negative result would isolate an additional law of relational iteration.
status_note: The 2018 source poses relative axiomatization as an open direction, and the December 2025 paper continues to distinguish axiomatization questions from its decidable full-signature theory. This card explicitly fixes a closure-free full-signature base and finitary induction rules as the concrete editorial variant. No completeness or incompleteness theorem for that exact system was located in the bounded 13 September 2026 check.

importance.reason: A substantial algebraic completeness question for relational reachability, sharpening the distinction between deciding identities and explaining them through reusable finitary proof principles.

sentences: Expressions denote binary relations using positive operations, converse and finite-path closure.
The target asks whether every relationally valid equation follows from a specified proof system.
That system contains all valid closure-free equations and ordinary left and right Kleene induction.
The closure-free base is an explicit editorial choice that fixes interactions among the operations.
The later EXPSPACE validity algorithm and completeness of smaller fragments do not prove this relative-completeness claim.

definitions: Expressions are finite terms over countably many relation variables using binary operations \(+\) (union), \(\cap\) (intersection), \(\cdot\) (composition), unary converse \((-)^{\circ}\), unary closure \((-)^*\), and constants \(0,1,\top\). On any set \(X\), variables denote arbitrary subsets of \(X\times X\). The constants denote the empty relation, the identity relation and \(X\times X\). Composition is \(R\cdot S=\{(x,z):\exists y\in X,\ (x,y)\in R\text{ and }(y,z)\in S\}\). Converse reverses each ordered pair. Closure is \(R^*=\bigcup_{n\geq0}R^n\), with \(R^0=1\) and \(R^{n+1}=R\cdot R^n\); it contains paths of every finite length, including zero. Complements and tests are absent. An equation is valid if it holds for every set \(X\), finite or infinite, and every assignment of its relation variables. Define \(u\leq v\) as the equation \(u+v=v\). The base axiom scheme consists of every valid equation whose expressions have no occurrence of \((-)^*\); it includes the interactions between union, intersection, converse and the constants. The Kleene algebra axioms make \((+,\cdot,0,1)\) an idempotent semiring: addition is associative, commutative and idempotent with identity zero; multiplication is associative with identity one, distributes over addition on both sides and has absorbing zero. The closure axioms are \(1+xx^*\leq x^*\) and \(1+x^*x\leq x^*\). The left induction rule infers \(x^*y\leq z\) from \(y+xz\leq z\); the right rule infers \(yx^*\leq z\) from \(y+zx\leq z\). Proofs are finite derivations using these schemes and rules, equality reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity, congruence for every operation, and uniform substitution of arbitrary expressions for variables. In particular, closure-bearing expressions may be substituted into closure-free axiom schemes. No other closure axiom, infinitary rule, relational-validity oracle for closure-bearing expressions or auxiliary operation is permitted.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof that this specified derivation system proves every relationally valid equation. Alternatively exhibit a valid equation and prove in Lean that it is not derivable in this system, for example using a model of all the axioms that refutes it. Decidability of relational validity alone, or a complete axiomatization of a proper signature fragment, does not establish completeness of these particular rules.

context_blocks.text: The source asks for axiomatizations and suggests adding Kleene algebra axioms to a complete closure-free relational calculus. Editorial specification: this card uses all valid closure-free laws in the full positive signature as the base. This explicitly includes interactions between union and intersection rather than leaving the interface between separate axiom systems ambiguous.

Without the specified base and rules, asking for an axiomatization would be too loose: declaring every valid equation an axiom gives no structural explanation. The target instead asks whether ordinary finitary Kleene induction accounts for all additional identities created by closure once the closure-free theory is available.

Intersection requires the same pair of endpoints to satisfy two relational conditions. It cannot generally be pushed through composition: \(R\cdot(S\cap T)\subseteq (R\cdot S)\cap(R\cdot T)\), but the reverse inclusion can fail because the two right-hand paths may use different intermediate points. Such interactions make relational closure more subtle than independent word-language iteration.

The 2018 paper records complete axiomatizations for important smaller signatures and explains why finite axiomatization of representable allegories is already delicate without closure. The target here deliberately permits an infinite closure-free axiom scheme and asks for relative completeness, rather than promising a finite list of all relational axioms.

Nakamura’s December 2025 journal article proves EXPSPACE-completeness of validity for the full positive signature, including identity, top, converse and closure. Its final discussion still distinguishes axiomatizability from the decision procedure. Thus an effective validity test does not by itself verify the relative proof system specified here.

The same later article cites a finite axiomatization for identity-free Kleene lattices. That result omits operations present in this card. It is retained as a boundary of known completeness results, not generalized to the full signature.
